name: Tee 5-Ball Progression
short_description: Five tee swings per round with one cue rotation. Logs hard-hit rate.
long_description: Hitter takes 5 swings off a tee per round, rotating one cue per round (e.g., 'load', 'see contact', 'finish'). Coach or partner logs each ball as hard-hit, soft, or miss. Two rounds = 10 swings.
setup_steps: Place tee at hitter's front hip
Set 5 balls in a bucket within reach
execution_steps: Hitter takes 5 swings using the round's single cue
Partner logs result of each swing

variations.name: Cue ladder
variations.change: Each round adds a different cue

author: platform

kid_friendly.explain: Five swings off the tee. Each round you only think about ONE thing — load, see contact, or finish — then we score how many are hard-hit.
kid_friendly.goal: Hit at least 3 out of 5 on the barrel. Loud sound, ball jumps off the tee, you finish balanced.
kid_friendly.why: Your body learns one cue at a time. In a game your brain only has time for one thought before the pitch — this is how we practice that.

name: Front Toss Take-or-Swing (5 pitches)
short_description: Coach calls 'take' or 'swing' mid-toss; hitter executes correctly.
long_description: Coach front-tosses 5 pitches per round. As the ball leaves coach's hand, coach calls 'take' or 'swing'. Hitter must execute the called action and only swing at strikes. Logs decision accuracy and hard-hit rate on swings.
setup_steps: Set L-screen at proper distance for age
execution_steps: Coach front-tosses pitch and calls 'take' or 'swing' on release
common_mistakes: Swinging at balls when 'take' was called and pitch was a ball

progressions.change: call replaced by colored ball (red=take, white=swing)

variations.name: Pitch-type decision
variations.change: two-pitch mix (FB/CH); hitter calls pitch and decision

author: platform

kid_friendly.explain: I’ll yell ‘swing’ or ‘take’ right when I let the ball go. Your job: do what I called, and only swing at strikes.
kid_friendly.goal: Get the call right 4 out of 5 times. When you swing, hit it hard.
kid_friendly.why: Hitters who chase pitches make outs. This trains your eyes to read the pitch BEFORE your hands decide. That’s how you walk more and crush mistakes.

name: Home-to-First Timed Run
short_description: Standardized home-to-first run with light gates or stopwatch.
long_description: Athlete starts in batter's box, makes a contact-style swing, drops bat in marked zone, runs through first base. Time recorded from contact-equivalent cue to first-base touch. Two reps, full recovery.
setup_steps: Mark batter's box and bat-drop zone
common_mistakes: Throwing the bat outside drop zone
author: platform

kid_friendly.explain: From the batter’s box, take your swing, drop the bat in the box, and SPRINT through first base. We time both runs.
kid_friendly.goal: Run THROUGH the bag — don’t slow down at first. Try to beat your own time on the second rep.
kid_friendly.why: In a real game, beating out a ground ball is the difference between an out and a hit. The fastest 30 feet of your life happens after contact.

name: Catcher Pop Time to 2B
short_description: Standardized pop time measurement, ball receipt to glove-touch at 2B.
long_description: Catcher receives a thrown pitch and executes throw to second base. Time from ball hitting catcher's glove to ball touching middle infielder's glove at 2B is logged. Three attempts, full recovery between.
execution_steps: Time recorded from glove pop to glove pop
coaching_cues: Receive to throw — no extra steps

variations.name: Pop to 3B
variations.change: Throw to third base on bunt fake

author: platform

kid_friendly.explain: Catch the pitch, no extra steps, fire it to second base. We time from when it hits your mitt to when it hits the middle infielder’s glove.
kid_friendly.goal: Catch-to-throw in one smooth motion. Stop a runner stealing — that’s the test.
kid_friendly.why: Pop time is how scouts measure catchers. Every tenth of a second you save is a runner you can throw out.

name: Reaction Ball Partner Catch
short_description: Bounce reaction ball to partner; track catches in 60 sec.
long_description: Partners stand 8-10 ft apart. One partner bounces a reaction ball off a flat surface to the other. Partner attempts to catch as many as possible in 60 seconds. Switch roles. Logs catches per 60 sec.
author: platform

kid_friendly.explain: This ball bounces crazy on purpose. Bounce it to your partner — they have to catch it however it comes off the floor. Count how many you catch in a minute.
kid_friendly.goal: Beat your last score. Stay low, soft hands, eyes on the ball the whole way.
kid_friendly.why: Ground balls and short hops never come the same way twice. Training your eyes and hands to react fast is what turns errors into outs.

name: 8-Minute Dynamic Warmup
short_description: Standard dynamic warmup gating any throwing or speed work.
long_description: 8-minute dynamic warmup sequence: jog, skips, lateral shuffles, leg swings, lunges, inchworms, arm circles, and band pull-aparts. Must complete before throwing or speed assessments.
author: platform

kid_friendly.explain: Eight minutes of movement before we throw or sprint. Light jog, skips, leg swings, arm circles — wake everything up.
kid_friendly.goal: Break a light sweat. Feel loose, not tired. Nobody throws or runs full speed until this is done.
kid_friendly.why: Cold muscles get hurt. This is how we protect your arm and legs so you can train at full speed for years, not just one season.

name: Youth Strength Foundations Circuit
short_description: Bodyweight + light load circuit: squat, hinge, push, pull, carry.
long_description: Five-station circuit: goblet squat (light), kettlebell deadlift (light), push-up, inverted row, suitcase carry. 3 rounds x 10-15 reps per station. Technique-first. Supervised. No 1RM.
author: platform

kid_friendly.explain: Five stations: squat, deadlift, push-up, row, carry. Light weight. Move slow and clean. Form before weight, every time.
kid_friendly.goal: Finish all three rounds with good form. If your back rounds or you wobble, the weight is too heavy — drop it.
kid_friendly.why: Strong legs, hips, and core make you swing harder, throw harder, and stay healthy. We earn the weight by earning the technique.

name: Acceleration Sprints 10/20 yd
short_description: Short acceleration sprints with full recovery.
long_description: After dynamic warmup, athlete completes 4 x 10 yd sprints then 4 x 20 yd sprints. Full recovery between reps (≥ 45 sec at 10 yd, ≥ 75 sec at 20 yd). Quality over fatigue.
execution_steps: Sprint to cone at full effort

progressions.change: react to coach cue at start

author: platform

kid_friendly.explain: Sprint hard to the cone, walk all the way back, then go again. Every rep is full effort — no jogging, no half-speed.
kid_friendly.goal: Your last sprint should feel as fast as your first. If you’re fading, take more rest.
kid_friendly.why: Stealing a base, beating out a hit, chasing down a fly ball — every one is a short sprint from a dead start. This IS baseball speed.

name: Baserunning Reads — 3 Stations
short_description: Three baserunning decision stations: primary lead, secondary read, tag-up.
long_description: Three small stations train baserunning reads: (1) primary lead and back, (2) secondary lead off pitcher's first move, (3) tag-up read on fly ball depth. Coach or partner gives cues; athlete reacts and logs success rate.
author: platform

kid_friendly.explain: Three stations on the bases. At each one I’ll give you a cue — pitcher’s first move, fly ball depth, pickoff — and you make the right read.
kid_friendly.goal: Right read, right reaction, every time. Not the fastest runner — the smartest.
kid_friendly.why: You don’t need to be the fastest to take an extra base. Great baserunners SEE one thing earlier than everyone else. That’s what we’re training.

name: Infield Triangle Read
short_description: Coach hits 3 grounders per round; fielder shows triangle approach + read.
long_description: Coach fungoes 3 grounders per round (right, middle, left). Fielder demonstrates triangle approach, glove read, and accurate throw to first. Logs clean fields and on-target throws.
setup_steps: Set first baseman or target net
author: platform

kid_friendly.explain: Three ground balls per round — one to your right, one straight, one to your left. Field it clean, then make an accurate throw to first.
kid_friendly.goal: Glove down early, work THROUGH the ball, and put the throw chest-high to first.
kid_friendly.why: This is the most-repeated play in baseball. A clean ground ball plus a catchable throw equals an out — every single time.

name: 60-Second Mental Reset
short_description: Box-breath + cue word reset between pressure reps.
long_description: Between high-pressure reps (live AB, mound visit, error), athlete uses a 60-second sequence: 4-count breath in, 4-count hold, 4-count out, 4-count hold, 4 cycles, then states a chosen cue word. Coach reinforces effort/process language.
setup_steps: Athlete picks cue word at start of season

variations.name: Team reset
variations.change: Whole team breathes together between innings

author: platform

kid_friendly.explain: Bad pitch, error, strikeout? Step off, four big breaths, say your cue word, and we play the next pitch. That’s the whole routine.
kid_friendly.goal: Use it EVERY time something goes wrong. If you forget, your teammate reminds you. No shame, just reset.
kid_friendly.why: The last play is over. Carrying it into the next one is how a small mistake turns into a big inning. Pros reset in 30 seconds — so can you.

name: Heat-Day Hydration Check
short_description: Pre/post weigh-in and urine-color self-check on heat-index days.
long_description: On heat-index days (>85°F or facility-set threshold), athletes complete pre-practice weigh-in, first-morning urine-color self-check (private), and post-practice weigh-in. Compiler flags athletes who lose >2% body mass and triggers rehydration messaging to athlete and parent.
author: platform

kid_friendly.explain: Hot day — we weigh in before and after practice, and you check your own pee color (privately) against the chart. That tells us if you’re drinking enough.
kid_friendly.goal: Lose less than 2% of your body weight. Pee should be pale yellow, not dark.
kid_friendly.why: Dehydration makes you slower, weaker, and more likely to get hurt before you even notice. Your body is the best tool you’ve got — take care of it.

name: Bullpen — 15-Pitch Command Block
short_description: Short bullpen, 15 pitches with location targets, logs strike% and arm-zone count.
long_description: Pitcher throws 15 pitches off a mound (or flat ground for 6-8). Catcher sets target for fastball arm-side / glove-side / down. Coach logs strike%. All throws count toward Pitch Smart daily limit.
setup_steps: Coach with target paddle behind catcher
common_mistakes: Pitching to the catcher's body not the glove
author: platform

kid_friendly.explain: Short bullpen — 15 pitches. Catcher sets a glove, you hit it. Don’t worry about how hard, worry about where.
kid_friendly.goal: Land 9 of 15 in or on the target. Finish each pitch with your chest over your front knee.
kid_friendly.why: Pitchers who throw strikes get to keep pitching. Velo gets you noticed; command keeps you on the mound.

name: Pitcher Fielding — Cover First Base
short_description: Tap-and-cover footwork to first base on a grounder to the right side.
long_description: Coach rolls grounders to 1B; pitcher breaks off the mound on the correct path, runs to a spot 6 feet inside the bag, then turns up the line. First baseman feeds with a soft underhand toss. 6 reps each side of the rubber.
execution_steps: Pitcher breaks toward foul line then turns up
1B underhand toss; pitcher catches and tags inside of bag
coaching_cues: Catch the ball, then find the bag
common_mistakes: Running directly to bag (gets in 1B way)

variations.name: Comebacker
variations.change: Coach hits at pitcher; pitcher fields and throws to 1B

author: platform

kid_friendly.explain: Ball gets hit to the right side — your job is to beat the hitter to first base. Take a curved path so you don’t crash into the first baseman.
kid_friendly.goal: Catch the toss before you touch the bag, then run through the inside corner.
kid_friendly.why: Every season a few games end because a pitcher didn’t cover first. Quiet play, big difference.

name: Living-Room Dry Swings
short_description: 10 mirror swings at home, one cue per round, no ball.
long_description: Player stands in front of a mirror at home (or with parent watching) and takes 10 dry swings, focusing on one mechanical cue per round (load, stride, finish). No bat-on-ball; foot speed controlled.
execution_steps: 10 dry swings focusing on one cue
coaching_cues: Smooth, don’t wreck the living room
common_mistakes: Going full speed in tight space

progressions.change: Add a slow-motion video review after each round

regressions.change: Use a dowel instead of a bat

variations.name: Eyes-closed finish
variations.change: Take the swing, close eyes, hold finish 3s

author: platform

kid_friendly.explain: Stand in front of a mirror at home. Take 10 slow swings. Each round you only think about ONE thing.
kid_friendly.goal: Finish in the same balanced spot every single rep.
kid_friendly.why: Your brain learns the swing in slow motion, not at game speed. This is the cheat code pros use in the off-season.

name: Living-Room Grip & Forearm Builder
short_description: Towel squeezes and wrist curls at home, 3 sets, no equipment beyond a towel.
long_description: Player performs 3 sets of 15 towel squeezes per hand, then 3 sets of 12 wrist curls holding a water bottle. Builds bat-control and throwing forearm without weights.
setup_steps: Forearm flat on table, wrist over edge
execution_steps: Wrist curls with bottle, palm up then palm down
coaching_cues: Slow down on the way back
author: platform

kid_friendly.explain: Squeeze a rolled-up towel 15 times each hand, then do little wrist curls with a water bottle.
kid_friendly.goal: Finish all 6 sets without your forearms going totally floppy.
kid_friendly.why: Stronger hands = the bat doesn’t move on contact = more hard-hit balls. Cheapest hitting upgrade there is.

name: Living-Room Vision Tracking
short_description: Eye-tracking drill with a tossed ball of yarn — no equipment that can break things.
long_description: Parent or sibling tosses a yarn ball or sock-ball underhand from 6 feet. Player calls 'yes' or 'no' based on whether the ball would have been a strike crossing their imaginary plate. 20 reps.
common_mistakes: Watching the tosser's eyes not the ball

variations.name: Number ball
variations.change: Tosser writes 1/2/3 on yarn; player calls number after deciding

author: platform

kid_friendly.explain: Mom or dad tosses a soft yarn ball. You don’t swing — you just call 'yes, strike' or 'no, ball' before it lands.
kid_friendly.goal: Get 15 of 20 right. Decide early; don’t wait until the ball is past you.
kid_friendly.why: Hitting is mostly choosing the right pitch. Eyes train first; the swing follows.

name: Outfield Drop-Step Ladder
short_description: Drop-step + cross-over to a tagged spot, 8 reps each direction.
long_description: Outfielder starts in athletic stance. Coach points right or left; outfielder executes a drop-step with the called foot and sprints to a cone 15 feet away. Focus on the FIRST step direction.
setup_steps: Set 4 cones in diamond around starter
execution_steps: Coach points; outfielder drop-steps with same-side foot and sprints
common_mistakes: Step toward the ball with the wrong foot first

progressions.change: Coach throws a fly ball after the point

author: platform

kid_friendly.explain: Coach points left or right. Your first move is to turn that hip back and sprint — no backpedal, no false step.
kid_friendly.goal: First foot moves in the right direction on at least 12 of 16 reps.
kid_friendly.why: Routes in the outfield are decided in the first step. Wrong step = the ball drops; right step = you’re under it.

name: Outfield Line-Drive Reads
short_description: Coach fungoes line drives; OF calls 'in/out/over' at release.
long_description: Coach hits line drives with a fungo from short distance. Outfielder must verbalize 'in' (charge), 'out' (back), or 'over' (turn and run) at contact. 10 reps. Builds read time before route.
execution_steps: Coach hits; OF calls in/out/over at contact, then makes the play
common_mistakes: Calling after the ball is halfway there
author: platform

kid_friendly.explain: Coach hits a line drive. The second the bat touches the ball, you yell 'in,' 'out,' or 'over' before you take a step.
kid_friendly.goal: Get the right call out loud on at least 7 of 10 balls.
kid_friendly.why: Outfielders who guess wrong on the first read can’t recover. Train your eyes to read off the bat, not the flight.

name: Double-Play Turn — 4-6-3
short_description: 2B feeds SS at the bag, SS pivots and throws to 1B. 8 reps.
long_description: Coach hits to 2B; 2B flips/throws to SS covering the bag; SS receives, pivots inside the bag, and throws to 1B. Focus on footwork at the bag and getting rid of the ball cleanly.
coaching_cues: Catch and throw in one motion

progressions.change: Add a baserunner sliding into the bag (soft slide)

author: platform

kid_friendly.explain: Two grounder, one out at second, then fire to first. You and your partner work together — the feed has to be on the chest so the SS can catch and throw in one move.
kid_friendly.goal: Turn 5 of 8 cleanly. No bobbles, no off-balance throws.
kid_friendly.why: A double play is the fastest way out of a rally. Practiced teams turn them; teams that don’t practice it boot the ball.

name: Sacrifice Bunt — 5 Balls
short_description: 5 sac-bunts from front toss, target zone is fair territory near 3B line.
long_description: Coach front-tosses 5 strikes. Hitter squares early, holds bat at top of zone, catches the ball with the bat. Goal: ball stops in fair territory between mound and 3B line.
execution_steps: Catch ball with bat angled toward 3B line
coaching_cues: Bat at the top of the zone, never below
Soft hands — give with the pitch
author: platform

kid_friendly.explain: Square up early, hold the bat at the top of the strike zone, and ‘catch’ the ball with the bat — don’t poke at it. We want the ball stopped in fair ground near third base.
kid_friendly.goal: 3 of 5 bunts fair and out of the catcher’s reach.
kid_friendly.why: Moving a runner with a bunt is a small play that wins close games. Coaches trust kids who can do it.

name: Cutoff & Relay — 3-Man Chain
short_description: OF → cutoff → tag base. 3 reps each side.
long_description: Coach hits ball to outfielder; OF throws to a lined-up cutoff; cutoff turns glove-side and throws to tag base. Drill the chain at game pace.
setup_steps: Cutoff lined up between OF and tag base
execution_steps: Cutoff turns glove-side and throws to tag base
common_mistakes: OF throwing on the bounce too early
author: platform

kid_friendly.explain: Ball in the gap. Outfielder throws to the cutoff’s chest. Cutoff spins glove-side and fires to the base. Three throws, one chain.
kid_friendly.goal: 4 of 6 chains hit the cutoff’s chest cleanly.
kid_friendly.why: Big throws from the outfield are slower and less accurate than a perfect relay. Teams that relay well keep doubles from becoming triples.

name: Catcher Framing — Low Strike
short_description: 20 low pitches, catcher works the bottom-of-zone receive.
long_description: Coach throws 20 pitches at the bottom of the strike zone. Catcher receives quietly with thumb up and slight upward presentation. Filmed for self-review.
coaching_cues: Quiet body, present the ball, don’t pull
common_mistakes: Pulling the glove up after the catch
author: platform

kid_friendly.explain: 20 low pitches. You receive quietly with your thumb up. Don’t pull the ball up — present it, hold it, give the ump a beat.
kid_friendly.goal: 14 of 20 caught quiet, no glove pull.
kid_friendly.why: Umpires reward catchers who don’t move. Steal a few low strikes a game and you save your pitcher’s arm.

name: Catcher Blocking — 3-Ball Sequence
short_description: 3 short-hop balls in a row: left, right, middle. 4 rounds.
long_description: Coach throws 3 short-hop balls in sequence at left, middle, right. Catcher drops to knees, angles hips toward middle, smothers ball with body. Recovery between sequences.
common_mistakes: Catching with glove instead of blocking
author: platform

kid_friendly.explain: Three short-hops in a row — left, right, middle. Knees down, chin tucked, ball stays in front of you.
kid_friendly.goal: Keep 9 of 12 balls within 3 feet of you.
kid_friendly.why: Catchers who block keep runners from stealing free bases. Pitchers throw braver when they trust you back there.

name: Bases-Loaded Live Situation
short_description: Coach hits live; defense reacts to runners and outs. 6 scenarios.
long_description: Set runners at all 3 bases. Coach declares outs (0, 1, or 2) and hits a live grounder or fly. Defense must throw to the right base. 6 scenarios with debrief after each.
execution_steps: Coach calls outs and hits live
coaching_cues: Know the outs before the pitch
Get one for sure, then look for two

progressions.change: Add a wild card pitch (passed ball)

author: platform

kid_friendly.explain: Bases loaded. Coach yells the outs, then hits the ball. You all have to know — before the pitch — where you’re throwing if the ball comes to you.
kid_friendly.goal: Make the right play on 4 of 6 scenarios.
kid_friendly.why: Most youth runs score on mental mistakes, not great hits. Knowing your job before the pitch is half the game.

name: 4-Corner Station Block (15 min)
short_description: Hit / field / throw / mobility stations, 3 min each, 1 min rotation.
long_description: Four stations: tee swings, soft-hands grounders, throwing accuracy, dynamic mobility. Groups of 2-4 rotate every 3 minutes. Keeps everyone moving — anti-line.
common_mistakes: Stations too far apart (wasted rotation time)

progressions.change: Add a 5th station; reduce time to 2 min each

author: platform

kid_friendly.explain: Four stations, 3 minutes each. Hit, field, throw, move. Coach blows the whistle — you rotate fast and don’t stand in line.
kid_friendly.goal: Hit all 4 stations. No more than 30 seconds of waiting at any one.
kid_friendly.why: You get better by doing reps, not watching them. We pack 4 skills into 15 minutes so nobody’s bored.

name: Reaction Light-Board (Partner Variation)
short_description: Partner flashes hand signals; you react with footwork. 30 reps.
long_description: Partner stands 6ft away and flashes hand signal (left/right/up/down). Athlete reacts with corresponding footwork: shuffle, drop-step, or jump. Measures reaction time and accuracy.
coaching_cues: Stay on the balls of your feet

progressions.change: Add a verbal cue that conflicts with the hand signal

author: platform

kid_friendly.explain: Partner shows a hand signal — left, right, up, down. You move that way as fast as you can. No guessing.
kid_friendly.goal: Get 24 of 30 right with no anticipation steps.
kid_friendly.why: Quick first move beats top speed every time. This is the same skill that turns singles into outs.

name: Tee — Oppo-Field 5
short_description: 5 tee swings driving the ball to the opposite field.
long_description: Tee placed slightly deeper in stance. Hitter swings 5 times trying to drive the ball to the opposite-field gap. Builds inside-out swing path.
execution_steps: 5 swings driving the ball to oppo gap
coaching_cues: Knob to the inside of the ball

progressions.change: Mix with pull-tee swings on alternating rounds

author: platform

kid_friendly.explain: Move the tee back a little. Try to hit all 5 to the opposite field. Hands stay inside the ball.
kid_friendly.goal: 3 of 5 line drives to the opposite gap.
kid_friendly.why: Hitters who can go the other way don’t get pitched around. It’s how you raise your batting average.

name: Soft-Hands Short-Hop
short_description: Partner rolls 20 short-hops; fielder uses bare hand or alligator-style glove.
long_description: Partner rolls 20 short-hops from 15 feet. Fielder catches with soft, low hands; ball into glove, top hand traps. Builds infield receiving.
execution_steps: Fielder catches with soft, low hands

variations.name: No glove
variations.change: Use bare hands; tennis balls only

author: platform

kid_friendly.explain: Partner rolls hard short-hops. Your job is to catch them soft — bring the ball to your belly button. Don’t stab.
kid_friendly.goal: Catch 16 of 20 clean. No double-clutches.
kid_friendly.why: Soft hands are the difference between an out and an error. This is the fundamental that infielders never outgrow.

name: Throwing Progression — Long Toss Build
short_description: Build from 30ft to comfortable max distance, then come back in. ~25 throws.
long_description: Partner throwing progression. Start at 30ft, move out every 5 throws until partner has to one-hop max distance. Then walk back in throwing on a line. Logged as a throwing day.
execution_steps: Walk back in, throwing on a line
common_mistakes: Arcing throws on the way back in
Throwing max distance when arm isn’t ready

progressions.change: Add a pulldown phase (5 max-effort throws)

author: platform

kid_friendly.explain: Start close with your partner, then back up every 5 throws until you’re at your max. Then walk back in throwing line drives.
kid_friendly.goal: Hit your partner’s chest at every distance. Walking back in, throws stay flat — no rainbows.
kid_friendly.why: Throwing far the right way builds a healthier, stronger arm. Throwing far the wrong way is how you blow out an elbow.
